```{r load-data, include=FALSE}
# Load SCFA and microbiome data following the logic in the source Rmd files,
# but with paths relative to the project root (one level up from this Rmd).

## SCFA: metadata and quantification data ---------------------------------

scfa_metadata <- NULL
scfa_sample_data_long <- NULL
scfa_sample_data_long_factored <- NULL

tryCatch({
  map1 <- read_excel(
    file.path("..", "scfa_metabolomics", "metadata", "SEED LAB HMM Submission Sheet 202405.xlsx"),
    skip = 9
  ) %>%
    clean_names()
  
  colnames(map1) <- c(
    "sampleid", "group", "bile_acids_panel", "pfbbr_scfa_panel",
    "tryp_indole_panel", "tms_panel_1", "tms_panel_2", "tms_panel_3",
    "untargeted_panel", "custom_targeted_panel", "low_abundant_metabolite_panel",
    "sample_origin", "sample_type", "mouse_number",
    "services_requested_per_sample", "mouse_strain", "mouse_flora",
    "volume_ul", "sample_weight_mg", "experiment_treatment"
  )
  
  map1 <- map1 %>%
    filter(!is.na(sampleid), sampleid != "") %>%
    slice(-(1:3))
  
  map2 <- read_excel(
    file.path("..", "scfa_metabolomics", "metadata", "PS2720_xtra_samples_HMM Submission Sheet.xlsx"),
    skip = 9
  ) %>%
    clean_names()
  
  colnames(map2) <- colnames(map1)
  
  map2 <- map2 %>%
    filter(!is.na(sampleid), sampleid != "") %>%
    slice(-(1:3))
  
  scfa_metadata_raw <- bind_rows(map1, map2)
}, error = function(e) {
  stop("Error reading SCFA metadata files: ", e$message)
})

scfa_metadata <- scfa_metadata_raw %>%
  mutate(
    subject = str_extract(sampleid, "^[0-9]+"),
    carb_repeat = str_extract(sampleid, "(?<= )[rs]\\d|nc(?= )"),
    carbohydrate_type = case_when(
      str_detect(carb_repeat, "^r") ~ "rapid_digestible",
      str_detect(carb_repeat, "^s") ~ "slow_digestible",
      str_detect(carb_repeat, "^nc") ~ "no_carbohydrate",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    technical_repeat = if_else(
      str_detect(carb_repeat, "^nc"),
      1L,
      as.integer(str_extract(carb_repeat, "\\d+"))
    ),
    timepoint_hr = as.integer(str_extract(sampleid, "(?<= )\\d+(?=h$)"))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(sampleid, group, subject, carbohydrate_type, technical_repeat, timepoint_hr) %>%
  mutate(group = tolower(group)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(group))

tryCatch({
  scfa_raw <- fread(
    file.path("..", "scfa_metabolomics", "data", "removed_qcs_quant_results_20250722_PFBBr_PS2720_20250731.csv")
  )
}, error = function(e) {
  stop("Error reading SCFA data file: ", e$message)
})

scfa_sample_data <- left_join(scfa_metadata, scfa_raw, by = "sampleid") %>%
  mutate(group = tolower(group)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(group))

scfa_analytes <- c("acetate", "butyrate", "propionate", "5aminovalerate", "succinate")

scfa_sample_data_long <- scfa_sample_data %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(scfa_analytes),
    names_to = "analyte",
    values_to = "concentration"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(concentration)) %>%
  group_by(subject, group, carbohydrate_type, timepoint_hr, analyte) %>%
  summarise(concentration = mean(concentration, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(
    group_label = factor(str_to_title(group), levels = c("Control", "Case")),
    carbohydrate_type_label = str_replace_all(carbohydrate_type, "_", " ") %>%
      str_to_title()
  )

scfa_sample_data_long_factored <- scfa_sample_data_long %>%
  mutate(
    group = factor(group, levels = c("control", "case")),
    carbohydrate_type = factor(
      carbohydrate_type,
      levels = c("no_carbohydrate", "rapid_digestible", "slow_digestible")
    ),
    timepoint_hr = factor(timepoint_hr),
    subject = factor(subject)
  )

## Microbiome: metadata, phyloseq, and relative abundances --------------

micro_metadata <- NULL
ps <- NULL
ps_rel <- NULL

tryCatch({
  micro_metadata_raw <- readr::read_tsv(
    file.path(
      "..", "microbiome_analysis", "zr24558.16S_250813.zymo",
      "00...AllSamples.Bac16Sv34", "Sample_Information", "sample.metadata.csv"
    ),
    show_col_types = FALSE
  ) %>%
    janitor::clean_names()
}, error = function(e) {
  stop("Error reading microbiome metadata file: ", e$message)
})

micro_metadata <- micro_metadata_raw %>%
  # Clean up double dots in labels like "NC..48H" and trim whitespace
  dplyr::mutate(
    customer_label = stringr::str_replace_all(customer_label, "\\.\\.", "."),
    customer_label = stringr::str_trim(customer_label)
  ) %>%
  separate(
    customer_label,
    into = c("subject_id", "replicate_code", "timepoint"),
    sep = "\\.",
    remove = FALSE
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    carbohydrate = case_when(
      stringr::str_detect(replicate_code, "R") ~ "RDC",
      stringr::str_detect(replicate_code, "S") ~ "SDC",
      TRUE ~ "No Added Carb"
    ),
    carbohydrate = factor(carbohydrate, levels = c("No Added Carb", "RDC", "SDC")),
    timepoint = factor(timepoint, levels = c("0H", "48H")),
    # Parse replicate number safely: treat NC as 1, numeric codes as their number
    replicate_code_clean = dplyr::if_else(
      stringr::str_detect(replicate_code, "NC"),
      NA_character_,
      replicate_code
    ),
    replicate = readr::parse_number(replicate_code_clean),
    replicate = tidyr::replace_na(replicate, 1L)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-replicate_code_clean) %>%
  dplyr::rename(SampleID = sample_id) %>%
  dplyr::select(SampleID, subject_id, customer_label, timepoint, carbohydrate, replicate, raw_seq_files)

tryCatch({
  healthy_lookup <- readr::read_tsv(
    file.path(
      "..", "microbiome_analysis", "zr24558.16S_250813.zymo",
      "1.Healthy.TimepointComparism..Bac16Sv34", "Sample_Information", "sample.metadata.csv"
    ),
    show_col_types = FALSE
  ) %>%
    janitor::clean_names() %>%
    separate(customer_label, into = c("subject_id", "tmp", "tp"), sep = "\\.", remove = FALSE) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(subject_id) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(group = "Healthy")
}, error = function(e) {
  stop("Error reading microbiome healthy lookup file: ", e$message)
})

micro_metadata <- micro_metadata %>%
  mutate(SampleID = paste0("S", customer_label)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    group = if_else(subject_id %in% healthy_lookup$subject_id, "Healthy", "Obese"),
    # Override MediaControl: group = NA, timepoint = "0H", carbohydrate = NA
    group = dplyr::if_else(
      stringr::str_detect(customer_label, regex("^MediaControl$", ignore_case = TRUE)),
      NA_character_,
      group
    ),
    timepoint = dplyr::if_else(
      stringr::str_detect(customer_label, regex("^MediaControl$", ignore_case = TRUE)),
      factor("0H", levels = levels(timepoint)),
      timepoint
    ),
    carbohydrate = dplyr::if_else(
      stringr::str_detect(customer_label, regex("^MediaControl$", ignore_case = TRUE)),
      factor(NA_character_, levels = levels(carbohydrate)),
      carbohydrate
    ),
    group = factor(group, levels = c("Healthy", "Obese")),
    subject_id = factor(subject_id)
  )

micro_metadata <- micro_metadata %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(timepoint))

tryCatch({
  ps <- import_biom(
    file.path(
      "..", "microbiome_analysis", "zr24558.16S_250813.zymo",
      "00...AllSamples.Bac16Sv34", "DADA2_ASV_Distribution", "ASV_Table.biom"
    )
  )
}, error = function(e) {
  stop("Error importing microbiome BIOM file: ", e$message)
})

colnames(tax_table(ps)) <- c("Kingdom", "Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus", "Species")

sample_names(ps) <- paste0("S", sample_names(ps))

metadata_ps <- micro_metadata %>%
  dplyr::mutate(SampleID = as.character(SampleID)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(SampleID) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(SampleID = if (n() > 1) paste0(SampleID, "_", row_number()) else SampleID) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  column_to_rownames("SampleID")

sample_data(ps) <- sample_data(metadata_ps)

ps <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(ps) > 0, ps)
ps <- prune_samples(sample_sums(ps) > 0, ps)

sample_data(ps)$SubjectID <- sample_data(ps)$subject_id
sample_data(ps)$Group <- sample_data(ps)$group
sample_data(ps)$Carbohydrate <- sample_data(ps)$carbohydrate
sample_data(ps)$Timepoint <- sample_data(ps)$timepoint

ps_rel <- microbiome::transform(ps, "compositional")

## qPCR absolute abundance data -----------------------------------------

qpcr_data <- NULL

tryCatch({
  qpcr_data <- readr::read_csv(
    file.path(
      "..", "microbiome_analysis", "zr24558.16S_250813.zymo",
      "00...AllSamples.Bac16Sv34", "Sample_Information", "absolute.abundance.csv"
    ),
    show_col_types = FALSE
  ) %>%
    janitor::clean_names()
}, error = function(e) {
  warning("Unable to load qPCR absolute abundance data: ", e$message)
})

# Note:
# - qPCR sample identifier column: customer_label
# - Will be joined to microbiome metadata via customer_label
# - genome_copies_per_ul will be used to convert relative to absolute
#   abundances in later sections.
```

# 1. Introduction

This integrated report brings together the short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) metabolomics and 16S rRNA gene microbiome analyses from the Lurie-Abbott carbohydrate obesity project. It re-runs the key components of each analysis within a single, reproducible R Markdown workflow and adds new integrative components relating taxa, SCFA concentrations, and responder phenotypes.

The goal is to maintain the rigor and depth of the original analyses while ensuring that metadata, filtering, and modeling decisions are harmonized across datasets.

# 2. Project Objectives

In this section, we summarize the main scientific and analytical objectives, building on the SCFA project objectives and extending them to explicitly include microbiome composition, diversity, and taxon–SCFA relationships.

# 3. Methods

This integrated analysis combines methods from both the SCFA metabolomics and 16S rRNA gene microbiome analyses. Below we describe the key methodological components employed throughout this report.

## 3.1 Study Design and Sample Processing

The study design includes two groups (Control/Healthy and Case/Obese) exposed to three carbohydrate conditions: no added carbohydrate (control), rapid digestible carbohydrate (RDC), and slow digestible carbohydrate (SDC). Samples were collected at multiple timepoints (0H, 48H, and 72H for SCFA; 0H and 48H for microbiome). All analyses account for repeated measures within subjects through appropriate statistical modeling.

## 3.2 SCFA Quantification and Preprocessing

Short-chain fatty acids (butyrate, propionate, acetate, and others) were quantified using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) with derivatization. Raw concentration data were preprocessed to remove quality control samples, handle missing values, and standardize units. Concentrations are reported in micromolar (μM) units. Data were log-transformed where appropriate for statistical analyses.

## 3.3 Microbiome Sequencing, Processing, and Phyloseq Construction

16S rRNA gene sequencing was performed on fecal samples, and sequences were processed through standard quality control, denoising, and taxonomic assignment pipelines. The processed data were organized into a `phyloseq` object containing an OTU/ASV table, taxonomic classifications, sample metadata, and phylogenetic tree information. Relative abundances were calculated by normalizing counts to proportions within each sample. Absolute abundances were derived by integrating qPCR-determined total bacterial genome copies per sample with relative abundance data.

## 3.4 Statistical Modeling Strategies

### 3.4.1 Mixed-Effects Models for SCFA Concentrations

Linear mixed-effects models were fitted using `lmerTest::lmer()` to analyze SCFA concentrations as a function of group (Control vs Case), carbohydrate type, timepoint, and their interactions, with random intercepts for subject to account for repeated measures. Type III ANOVA tables were generated using `anova()` to test main effects and interactions, with p-values adjusted for multiple comparisons using the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) false discovery rate (FDR) correction.

### 3.4.2 Alpha Diversity Analysis

Within-sample microbial diversity was assessed using three metrics: Observed richness (number of unique taxa), Shannon diversity index (accounts for both richness and evenness), and Simpson diversity index (emphasizes dominant taxa). Differences in alpha diversity between groups, carbohydrate conditions, and timepoints were tested using Wilcoxon rank-sum tests (Mann-Whitney U tests) with BH FDR correction for multiple comparisons.

### 3.4.3 Beta Diversity and Community Structure

Between-sample microbial community dissimilarity was quantified using Bray-Curtis distance on relative abundance data. Principal coordinates analysis (PCoA) was used to visualize community structure in reduced dimensions. Permutational multivariate analysis of variance (PERMANOVA) using `vegan::adonis2()` with 999 permutations was employed to test for significant differences in community composition between groups, carbohydrate conditions, and timepoints, with subject ID as a stratification variable to account for repeated measures.

### 3.4.4 Differential Abundance Analysis

Two complementary methods were used to identify taxa that differ significantly between conditions:

**ANCOM-BC2**: Analysis of Compositions of Microbiomes with Bias Correction 2 was applied using the `ANCOMBC` package. This method accounts for compositionality and provides log-fold change estimates with bias correction, standard errors, and FDR-adjusted q-values. Models included group, carbohydrate, timepoint, and their interactions as fixed effects, with subject ID as a random effect where appropriate.

**MaAsLin2**: Microbiome Multivariable Association with Linear Models 2 was applied using the `Maaslin2` package. This method uses linear models with total sum scaling (TSS) normalization and log transformation. It provides coefficient estimates, standard errors, p-values, and FDR-adjusted q-values. Models included the same fixed and random effects as ANCOM-BC2 analyses.

Both methods were applied to relative abundance data, and results were filtered to retain associations with q < 0.1 (FDR-adjusted p-value threshold).

### 3.4.5 Taxon–SCFA Association Analysis

To identify microbial taxa associated with SCFA concentrations, ANCOM-BC2 and MaAsLin2 were applied with butyrate or propionate concentrations as continuous predictors, along with carbohydrate type and their interactions. These analyses were performed on relative abundance data and included subject ID as a random effect to account for repeated measures.

### 3.4.6 Correlation Analyses

Spearman rank correlation coefficients were calculated to assess monotonic relationships between taxon abundances (e.g., *Fusicatenibacter*) and SCFA concentrations. Linear regression models were fitted to estimate R² values and test for linear associations. Correlations were examined at specific timepoints (e.g., 48H) and carbohydrate conditions (e.g., SDC only) to focus on biologically relevant contexts.

### 3.4.7 Responder vs Non-Responder Classification

Responder status was defined separately for butyrate and propionate based on the change in SCFA concentration from baseline (0H) to 48H (delta = 48H - 0H). For each analyte and carbohydrate condition, samples were classified as "Responder" if their delta value was greater than or equal to the median delta, and "Non-Responder" if below the median. This data-driven threshold allows for identification of individuals who show a substantial SCFA response to carbohydrate challenge relative to their peers in the same condition.

### 3.4.8 Responder Group Comparisons

Microbial composition differences between responder and non-responder groups were assessed using:
- Alpha diversity comparisons with Wilcoxon rank-sum tests
- Beta diversity comparisons using PERMANOVA
- Differential abundance analysis using ANCOM-BC2 and MaAsLin2 to identify taxa that differ between responder and non-responder groups

## 3.5 Integration Methods

SCFA and microbiome data were integrated by matching samples based on subject ID, timepoint, and carbohydrate condition. Metadata were harmonized to ensure consistent group labels (Control/Healthy, Case/Obese) and carbohydrate labels (No Added Carb, RDC, SDC) across datasets. The integrated metadata were added to the phyloseq object's sample data component to enable joint analyses.

## 3.6 Visualization and Reporting

All visualizations were created using `ggplot2` with a consistent color palette and theme derived from the SCFA analysis. Forest plots display effect sizes (log-fold changes) with 95% confidence intervals for ANCOM-BC2 results. Volcano plots show effect sizes versus significance for MaAsLin2 results. Alluvial diagrams illustrate compositional changes over time. Statistical test results are displayed directly on plots where appropriate (e.g., Wilcoxon p-values on boxplots, R² values on scatter plots). All p-values are reported with FDR adjustment where multiple comparisons were performed.


# 4. Summary Data

We begin with a concise overview of the sample counts by obesity status (Control vs Case) and carbohydrate condition across both SCFA and microbiome datasets.

```{r summary-data, echo=FALSE}
# Summary counts for SCFA (control/case) and microbiome (Healthy/Obese)

# SCFA: deduplicate to one row per biological sample (subject × timepoint × carbohydrate)
scfa_sample_overview <- scfa_sample_data_long_factored %>%
  dplyr::distinct(subject, group, carbohydrate_type, timepoint_hr) %>%
  mutate(
    group_label = factor(str_to_title(group), levels = c("Control", "Case")),
    carbohydrate = case_when(
      carbohydrate_type == "no_carbohydrate" ~ "No Added Carb",
      carbohydrate_type == "rapid_digestible" ~ "RDC",
      carbohydrate_type == "slow_digestible" ~ "SDC",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    carbohydrate = factor(carbohydrate, levels = c("No Added Carb", "RDC", "SDC"))
  )

scfa_summary_counts <- scfa_sample_overview %>%
  dplyr::count(group_label, carbohydrate, name = "n_samples") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(group_label, carbohydrate)

# Microbiome: sample counts by group and carbohydrate (all timepoints)
micro_summary_counts <- micro_metadata %>%
  dplyr::count(group, carbohydrate, timepoint, name = "n_samples") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(group, carbohydrate, timepoint)

scfa_table <- scfa_summary_counts %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    Group = group_label,
    Carbohydrate = carbohydrate,
    `N samples` = n_samples
  )

micro_table <- micro_summary_counts %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    Group = group,
    Carbohydrate = carbohydrate,
    Timepoint = timepoint,
    `N samples` = n_samples
  )

# Print SCFA table
if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
  DT::datatable(
    scfa_table,
    caption = "SCFA samples by group and carbohydrate",
    options = list(pageLength = 10, dom = "tip"),
    rownames = FALSE
  )
} else {
  knitr::kable(scfa_table, caption = "SCFA samples by group and carbohydrate")
}

# Print Microbiome table
if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
  DT::datatable(
    micro_table,
    caption = "Microbiome samples by group, carbohydrate, and timepoint",
    options = list(pageLength = 10, dom = "tip"),
    rownames = FALSE
  )
} else {
  knitr::kable(micro_table, caption = "Microbiome samples by group, carbohydrate, and timepoint")
}
```

# 5. Metabolomics (SCFA)

## 5.1 Section Overview

This section reproduces and extends the SCFA analyses, focusing on:

- Carbohydrate type effects (combined and stratified by group)
- SCFA concentrations over time
- Advanced mixed-effects modeling for SCFA trajectories

We first quantify SCFA response magnitudes (48h – 0h) and evaluate how they vary by carbohydrate type and obesity group. We then visualize SCFA concentrations over time and fit linear mixed-effects models with subject as a random effect to formally test fixed effects of group, carbohydrate type, time, and their interactions on absolute SCFA concentrations.

## 5.2 Carbohydrate Type Effects (Combined Groups)

```{r scfa-carbohydrate-effects-prep, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# Prepare data for all plots (shared across chunks)
delta_data <- scfa_sample_data_long_factored %>%
  dplyr::filter(timepoint_hr %in% c("0", "48")) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    id_cols = c(subject, group, carbohydrate_type, analyte, group_label, carbohydrate_type_label),
    names_from = timepoint_hr,
    values_from = concentration,
    names_prefix = "time_"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(delta_48h_0h = time_48 - time_0) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(delta_48h_0h))

# One-way ANOVA on delta by carbohydrate type (combined groups)
combined_carb_stats <- purrr::map_dfr(
  unique(delta_data$analyte),
  function(analyte_name) {
    analyte_data <- delta_data %>% dplyr::filter(analyte == analyte_name)
    model <- aov(delta_48h_0h ~ carbohydrate_type, data = analyte_data)
    anova_summary <- summary(model)[[1]]
    data.frame(
      analyte = analyte_name,
      Effect = rownames(anova_summary),
      DF = anova_summary$Df,
      Sum_Sq = anova_summary$`Sum Sq`,
      Mean_Sq = anova_summary$`Mean Sq`,
      F_value = anova_summary$`F value`,
      p = anova_summary$`Pr(>F)`
    ) %>%
      dplyr::filter(Effect != "Residuals") %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        p_adj = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"),
        significance = dplyr::case_when(
          p_adj < 0.001 ~ "p<0.001",
          p_adj < 0.01 ~ "p<0.01",
          p_adj < 0.05 ~ "p<0.05",
          TRUE ~ "ns"
        )
      )
  }
)
```

### 5.2.1 Control Group: Delta SCFA by Carbohydrate Type

```{r scfa-carbohydrate-effects-control, echo=FALSE, fig.width=14, fig.height=8}
# Control group-specific delta plot
plot_delta_control_only <- tryCatch({
  delta_data %>%
    dplyr::filter(group == "control") %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = carbohydrate_type_label, y = delta_48h_0h)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50", alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_boxplot(aes(fill = carbohydrate_type_label), alpha = 0.8, outlier.shape = NA) +
    geom_jitter(alpha = 0.6, width = 0.2, size = 1.5, color = "gray30") +
    facet_wrap(~ analyte, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_fill_scfa() +
    ggpubr::stat_compare_means(
      comparisons = list(
        c("No Carbohydrate", "Rapid Digestible"),
        c("No Carbohydrate", "Slow Digestible"),
        c("Rapid Digestible", "Slow Digestible")
      ),
      method = "wilcox.test",
      label = "p.signif",
      step.increase = 0.1
    ) +
    labs(
      title = "SCFA Response Magnitude by Carbohydrate Type - Control Group Only",
      subtitle = "Delta change (48h - 0h) with Wilcoxon pairwise comparisons",
      x = "Carbohydrate Type",
      y = "Change in Concentration (48h - 0h) μM"
    ) +
    theme_scfa() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
}, error = function(e) {
  cat("Error creating plot_delta_control_only:", e$message, "\n")
  NULL
})

# Print plot explicitly
if (!is.null(plot_delta_control_only)) {
  print(plot_delta_control_only)
} else {
  cat("Warning: plot_delta_control_only is NULL\n")
}
```

### 5.2.2 Case Group: Delta SCFA by Carbohydrate Type

```{r scfa-carbohydrate-effects-case, echo=FALSE, fig.width=14, fig.height=8}
# Case group-specific delta plot
plot_delta_case_only <- tryCatch({
  delta_data %>%
    dplyr::filter(group == "case") %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = carbohydrate_type_label, y = delta_48h_0h)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50", alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_boxplot(aes(fill = carbohydrate_type_label), alpha = 0.8, outlier.shape = NA) +
    geom_jitter(alpha = 0.6, width = 0.2, size = 1.5, color = "gray30") +
    facet_wrap(~ analyte, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_fill_scfa() +
    ggpubr::stat_compare_means(
      comparisons = list(
        c("No Carbohydrate", "Rapid Digestible"),
        c("No Carbohydrate", "Slow Digestible"),
        c("Rapid Digestible", "Slow Digestible")
      ),
      method = "wilcox.test",
      label = "p.signif",
      step.increase = 0.1
    ) +
    labs(
      title = "SCFA Response Magnitude by Carbohydrate Type - Case Group Only",
      subtitle = "Delta change (48h - 0h) with Wilcoxon pairwise comparisons",
      x = "Carbohydrate Type",
      y = "Change in Concentration (48h - 0h) μM"
    ) +
    theme_scfa() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
}, error = function(e) {
  cat("Error creating plot_delta_case_only:", e$message, "\n")
  NULL
})

# Print plot explicitly
if (!is.null(plot_delta_case_only)) {
  print(plot_delta_case_only)
} else {
  cat("Warning: plot_delta_case_only is NULL\n")
}
```

## 5.4 Advanced Statistical Modeling: Mixed-Effects Models

```{r scfa-mixed-effects, echo=FALSE}
# Mixed-effects models for absolute SCFA concentrations
mixed_effects_results <- scfa_sample_data_long_factored %>%
  dplyr::group_by(analyte) %>%
  tidyr::nest() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    # Use lmerTest::lmer so that anova() returns F-tests with p-values
    model = purrr::map(
      data,
      ~ lmerTest::lmer(
        concentration ~ group * carbohydrate_type * timepoint_hr + (1 | subject),
        data = .x
      )
    ),
    anova_main = purrr::map(model, ~ anova(.x)),
    model_summary = purrr::map(model, ~ summary(.x))
  )

main_anova_summary <- mixed_effects_results %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    anova_df = purrr::map(
      anova_main,
      ~ as.data.frame(.x) %>%
        tibble::rownames_to_column("effect")
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(analyte, anova_df) %>%
  tidyr::unnest(anova_df) %>%
  dplyr::filter(effect != "Residual") %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    F_value = `F value`,
    pr_f = `Pr(>F)`
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    p_adj = p.adjust(pr_f, method = "BH"),
    significance = dplyr::case_when(
      p_adj < 0.001 ~ "p<0.001",
      p_adj < 0.01 ~ "p<0.01",
      p_adj < 0.05 ~ "p<0.05",
      TRUE ~ "ns"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(p_adj)

if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
  DT::datatable(
    main_anova_summary %>%
      dplyr::select(analyte, effect, F_value, pr_f, p_adj, significance),
    caption = "Mixed-Effects Models for SCFA Concentrations: ANOVA Table",
    options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE),
    rownames = FALSE
  ) %>%
    DT::formatRound(columns = c("F_value", "pr_f", "p_adj"), digits = 4)
} else {
  knitr::kable(
    main_anova_summary %>%
      dplyr::select(analyte, effect, F_value, pr_f, p_adj, significance),
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Mixed-Effects Models for SCFA Concentrations: ANOVA Table"
  )
}
```

## 5.5 Summary of SCFA Results

The SCFA metabolomics analysis reveals several key findings regarding short-chain fatty acid production in response to carbohydrate challenge in adolescents with and without obesity:

**1. Dominant Effect of Carbohydrate Type and Time**

The primary drivers of SCFA production in this ex vivo model were the type of carbohydrate supplied and the incubation time. Both rapid digestible carbohydrate (RDC) and slow digestible carbohydrate (SDC) led to significant increases in all measured SCFAs (butyrate, propionate, acetate) over 48 hours compared to the no-carbohydrate control. This was confirmed by:
- Significant differences in delta changes (48H - 0H) between carbohydrate conditions across multiple SCFAs (Section 5.2)
- Clear temporal increases in SCFA concentrations over time, with distinct trajectories for each carbohydrate type (Section 5.3)
- Robust statistical significance in the mixed-effects models, where carbohydrate type and timepoint consistently emerged as significant main effects and interactions (Section 5.4)

**2. Subtle Differences Between Case and Control Groups**

While there were some minor differences in baseline SCFA levels and response patterns between the case (obesity) and control groups, the overall response to carbohydrate interventions was remarkably similar. The mixed-effects models showed limited significant main effects of `group` or major interactions involving `group`, suggesting that the fundamental capacity of the gut microbiota to ferment these carbohydrates is not dramatically altered in the context of obesity in this cohort. This finding suggests that obesity status alone does not substantially impair the microbial fermentation capacity for these carbohydrate substrates.

**3. Carbohydrate-Specific Response Patterns**

The analyses revealed distinct response patterns for different carbohydrate types:
- Both RDC and SDC stimulated SCFA production compared to no-carbohydrate controls
- The magnitude and timing of responses varied by carbohydrate type, as evidenced by significant carbohydrate × timepoint interactions in the mixed-effects models
- These differences highlight the importance of carbohydrate structure and digestibility in shaping microbial metabolic output

**4. Pronounced Interpersonal Variation**

A central finding is the high degree of subject-to-subject variability in SCFA production. The delta change analyses (Section 5.2) and temporal trajectories (Section 5.3) clearly demonstrate that:
- Some individuals are consistently high or low SCFA producers across conditions
- Response patterns to different carbohydrates are unique to each individual
- This variability is evident even when accounting for group (case vs control) and carbohydrate type effects

This pronounced interpersonal variation underscores the need for personalized approaches in nutrition, as a "one-size-fits-all" dietary intervention is unlikely to be effective. The identification of responder and non-responder groups (explored in Section 7) builds upon this finding to enable more targeted analyses of microbial composition differences.

**5. Statistical Model Insights**

The linear mixed-effects models (Section 5.4) provide formal statistical confirmation of these patterns, accounting for repeated measures within subjects. Key model findings include:
- Significant main effects of carbohydrate type and timepoint across multiple SCFAs
- Significant interactions between carbohydrate type and timepoint, indicating that the temporal response depends on the carbohydrate substrate
- Limited group effects, consistent with the observation that obesity status does not dramatically alter fermentation capacity
- The models account for subject-level variation through random intercepts, capturing the interpersonal differences observed in the data

These findings set the stage for the integrated analyses in Section 7, where we examine how microbial composition relates to SCFA production patterns and identify specific taxa associated with SCFA concentrations and responder phenotypes.

# 6. Microbiome

## 6.1 Section Overview

This section reproduces key microbiome results, including alpha and beta diversity, community composition, and differential abundance, using the harmonized metadata and styling. We focus first on within-sample diversity (alpha diversity) to summarize richness and evenness patterns across groups, carbohydrate conditions, and timepoints, then move to between-sample diversity (beta diversity) and taxon-level changes.

## 6.2 Alpha Diversity

```{r alpha-diversity, echo=FALSE, fig.width=18, fig.height=8}
  tibble::rownames_to_column("SampleID")

    cols = -SampleID,

  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Alpha Diversity by Group, Carbohydrate, and Timepoint",

    y = "Diversity metric"
  ) +
  theme_scfa() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# Summaries at 48H for combined groups modeling
alpha_48h <- alpha_long %>%
  dplyr::filter(timepoint == "48H")

alpha_48h_summary <- alpha_48h %>%
  dplyr::group_by(metric, group, carbohydrate) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Wilcoxon tests: Healthy vs Obese within carbohydrate × timepoint for each alpha metric
alpha_wilcox_group <- tryCatch({
  alpha_long_0_48 %>%
    dplyr::group_by(metric, carbohydrate, timepoint) %>%
    dplyr::filter(dplyr::n_distinct(group) == 2) %>%  # Only test if both groups present
    rstatix::wilcox_test(value ~ group, p.adjust.method = "BH") %>%
    rstatix::add_significance() %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()
}, error = function(e) {
  cat("Error calculating alpha_wilcox_group:", e$message, "\n")
  tibble::tibble()
})

# Check available columns and select appropriate ones
if (nrow(alpha_wilcox_group) > 0) {
  # Check what columns exist (p.adj vs p_adjust)
  p_adj_col <- intersect(c("p.adj", "p_adjust", "adj.p.value"), names(alpha_wilcox_group))
  p_adj_col <- if (length(p_adj_col) > 0) p_adj_col[1] else NULL
  
  p_signif_col <- intersect(c("p.adj.signif", "p_adjust_signif", "signif"), names(alpha_wilcox_group))
  p_signif_col <- if (length(p_signif_col) > 0) p_signif_col[1] else NULL
  
  # Create adjusted p-value if it doesn't exist
  if (is.null(p_adj_col) && "p" %in% names(alpha_wilcox_group)) {
    alpha_wilcox_group$p_adj <- p.adjust(alpha_wilcox_group$p, method = "BH")
  } else if (!is.null(p_adj_col)) {
    alpha_wilcox_group$p_adj <- alpha_wilcox_group[[p_adj_col]]
  } else {
    alpha_wilcox_group$p_adj <- NA_real_
  }
  
  # Create significance column if it doesn't exist
  if (is.null(p_signif_col)) {
    alpha_wilcox_group$p_adj_signif <- dplyr::case_when(
      alpha_wilcox_group$p_adj < 0.001 ~ "***",
      alpha_wilcox_group$p_adj < 0.01 ~ "**",
      alpha_wilcox_group$p_adj < 0.05 ~ "*",
      alpha_wilcox_group$p_adj < 0.1 ~ ".",
      TRUE ~ "ns"
    )
  } else {
    alpha_wilcox_group$p_adj_signif <- alpha_wilcox_group[[p_signif_col]]
  }
  
  alpha_wilcox_group <- alpha_wilcox_group %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      comparison = paste0(group1, " vs ", group2),
      metric_carb_time = paste(metric, carbohydrate, timepoint, sep = " | ")
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(metric, carbohydrate, timepoint, comparison, p, p_adj, p_adj_signif)
} else {
  alpha_wilcox_group <- tibble::tibble(
    metric = character(0),
    carbohydrate = character(0),
    timepoint = character(0),
    comparison = character(0),
    p = numeric(0),
    p_adj = numeric(0),
    p_adj_signif = character(0)
  )
}
```

## 6.3 Beta Diversity

```{r beta-diversity, echo=FALSE, fig.width=14, fig.height=10}
# Beta diversity and community structure using Bray-Curtis distance

# Helper: PCoA data frame
make_pcoa_df <- function(ps_obj, distance_method) {
  ord <- ordinate(ps_obj, method = "PCoA", distance = distance_method)
  vecs <- as_tibble(ord$vectors[, 1:2], rownames = "SampleID")
  colnames(vecs)[2:3] <- c("PC1", "PC2")
  vecs <- vecs %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      axis1_var = ord$values$Relative_eig[1],
      axis2_var = ord$values$Relative_eig[2]
    ) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      as_tibble(micro_metadata, .name_repair = "minimal"),
      by = "SampleID"
    )
  vecs
}

# Bray-Curtis PCoA across all samples
pcoa_bray <- make_pcoa_df(ps_rel, "bray")

# PERMANOVA: group × carbohydrate + timepoint with subject-level strata
dist_bray <- phyloseq::distance(ps_rel, method = "bray")
df_beta <- as(sample_data(ps_rel), "data.frame")

permanova_bray <- vegan::adonis2(
  dist_bray ~ group * carbohydrate + timepoint,
  data = df_beta,
  permutations = 999,
  strata = df_beta$subject_id
)

permanova_bray_tbl <- as.data.frame(permanova_bray) %>%
  rownames_to_column("term") %>%
  janitor::clean_names()

# Try to standardize column names for downstream use
permanova_bray_p_col <- intersect(
  c("pr_greater_f_", "pr_greater_f", "pr_f", "p_value"),
  names(permanova_bray_tbl)
)
permanova_bray_p_col <- if (length(permanova_bray_p_col) > 0) permanova_bray_p_col[1] else NULL

permanova_bray_f_col <- intersect(
  c("f", "f_model", "pseudo_f"),
  names(permanova_bray_tbl)
)
permanova_bray_f_col <- if (length(permanova_bray_f_col) > 0) permanova_bray_f_col[1] else NULL

permanova_bray_r2_col <- intersect(
  c("r2", "r_squared", "r2_adj"),
  names(permanova_bray_tbl)
)
permanova_bray_r2_col <- if (length(permanova_bray_r2_col) > 0) permanova_bray_r2_col[1] else NULL

# Create standardized columns if they don't exist
if (!is.null(permanova_bray_f_col)) {
  permanova_bray_tbl$f <- permanova_bray_tbl[[permanova_bray_f_col]]
} else if ("f" %in% names(permanova_bray_tbl)) {
  permanova_bray_tbl$f <- permanova_bray_tbl$f
} else {
  permanova_bray_tbl$f <- NA_real_
}

if (!is.null(permanova_bray_r2_col)) {
  permanova_bray_tbl$r2 <- permanova_bray_tbl[[permanova_bray_r2_col]]
} else if ("r2" %in% names(permanova_bray_tbl)) {
  permanova_bray_tbl$r2 <- permanova_bray_tbl$r2
} else {
  permanova_bray_tbl$r2 <- NA_real_
}

if (!is.null(permanova_bray_p_col)) {
  permanova_bray_tbl$p_value <- permanova_bray_tbl[[permanova_bray_p_col]]
} else if ("p_value" %in% names(permanova_bray_tbl)) {
  permanova_bray_tbl$p_value <- permanova_bray_tbl$p_value
} else {
  permanova_bray_tbl$p_value <- NA_real_
}

# PCoA plot with PERMANOVA annotation (R² and p for group:carbohydrate)
permanova_gc <- permanova_bray_tbl %>%
  dplyr::filter(term == "group:carbohydrate")

annotation_text <- NULL
if (nrow(permanova_gc) > 0 && !is.na(permanova_gc$r2[1]) && !is.na(permanova_gc$p_value[1])) {
  annotation_text <- as.character(glue::glue(
    "R² = {round(permanova_gc$r2[1], 3)}, p = {signif(permanova_gc$p_value[1], 3)}"
  ))
}

beta_pcoa_plot <- {
  p <- pcoa_bray %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = carbohydrate, shape = group)) +
    geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.85) +
    stat_ellipse(
      aes(group = interaction(carbohydrate, timepoint), color = carbohydrate),
      linewidth = 0.4,
      linetype = "dashed",
      show.legend = FALSE
    ) +
    facet_wrap(~timepoint) +
    scale_color_scfa() +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17)) +
    labs(
      x = paste0("PC1 (", scales::percent(round(pcoa_bray$axis1_var[1], 3)), ")"),
      y = paste0("PC2 (", scales::percent(round(pcoa_bray$axis2_var[1], 3)), ")"),
      title = "PCoA – Bray-Curtis distance"
    ) +
    theme_scfa()

  if (!is.null(annotation_text)) {
    p <- p +
      annotate(
        "label",
        x = -Inf,
        y = Inf,
        hjust = -0.05,
        vjust = 1.1,
        label = annotation_text,
        size = 3,
        fontface = "bold",
        fill = "white",
        alpha = 0.8
      )
  }

  p
}

# 48H-only Bray-Curtis PCoA and PERMANOVA
ps_48h <- phyloseq::subset_samples(ps_rel, Timepoint == "48H")
pcoa_48h <- make_pcoa_df(ps_48h, "bray")

dist_48h <- phyloseq::distance(ps_48h, method = "bray")
metadata_48h <- as(sample_data(ps_48h), "data.frame")

permanova_48h <- vegan::adonis2(
  dist_48h ~ group * carbohydrate,
  data = metadata_48h,
  permutations = 999,
  strata = metadata_48h$subject_id
)

permanova_48h_tbl <- as.data.frame(permanova_48h) %>%
  rownames_to_column("term") %>%
  janitor::clean_names()

permanova_48h_p_col <- intersect(
  c("pr_greater_f_", "pr_greater_f", "pr_f", "p_value"),
  names(permanova_48h_tbl)
)
permanova_48h_p_col <- if (length(permanova_48h_p_col) > 0) permanova_48h_p_col[1] else NULL

permanova_48h_f_col <- intersect(
  c("f", "f_model", "pseudo_f"),
  names(permanova_48h_tbl)
)
permanova_48h_f_col <- if (length(permanova_48h_f_col) > 0) permanova_48h_f_col[1] else NULL

permanova_48h_r2_col <- intersect(
  c("r2", "r_squared", "r2_adj"),
  names(permanova_48h_tbl)
)
permanova_48h_r2_col <- if (length(permanova_48h_r2_col) > 0) permanova_48h_r2_col[1] else NULL

# Create standardized columns if they don't exist
if (!is.null(permanova_48h_f_col)) {
  permanova_48h_tbl$f <- permanova_48h_tbl[[permanova_48h_f_col]]
} else if ("f" %in% names(permanova_48h_tbl)) {
  permanova_48h_tbl$f <- permanova_48h_tbl$f
} else {
  permanova_48h_tbl$f <- NA_real_
}

if (!is.null(permanova_48h_r2_col)) {
  permanova_48h_tbl$r2 <- permanova_48h_tbl[[permanova_48h_r2_col]]
} else if ("r2" %in% names(permanova_48h_tbl)) {
  permanova_48h_tbl$r2 <- permanova_48h_tbl$r2
} else {
  permanova_48h_tbl$r2 <- NA_real_
}

if (!is.null(permanova_48h_p_col)) {
  permanova_48h_tbl$p_value <- permanova_48h_tbl[[permanova_48h_p_col]]
} else if ("p_value" %in% names(permanova_48h_tbl)) {
  permanova_48h_tbl$p_value <- permanova_48h_tbl$p_value
} else {
  permanova_48h_tbl$p_value <- NA_real_
}

beta_pcoa_48h_plot <- pcoa_48h %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = carbohydrate, shape = group)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.9) +
  stat_ellipse(aes(group = carbohydrate, color = carbohydrate),
               linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_scfa() +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17)) +
  labs(
    x = paste0("PC1 (", scales::percent(round(pcoa_48h$axis1_var[1], 3)), ")"),
    y = paste0("PC2 (", scales::percent(round(pcoa_48h$axis2_var[1], 3)), ")"),
    title = "PCoA – Bray-Curtis distance (48H samples)"
  ) +
  theme_scfa()

# Print plots
print(beta_pcoa_plot)

# Print PERMANOVA table for all timepoints
if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
  DT::datatable(
    permanova_bray_tbl %>%

}

# Print 48H plot
```

## 6.4 Community Composition


### 6.4.1 Genus-Level Aggregation and Overview

```{r genus-aggregation, echo=FALSE, fig.width=14, fig.height=10}

genus_abundance <- sort(taxa_sums(ps_genus), decreasing = TRUE)
```

### 6.4.2 Genus Composition Changes from 0H to 48H by Carbohydrate Type

```{r genus-alluvial, echo=FALSE, fig.width=14, fig.height=10}
# Prepare data for alluvial diagrams showing flow from 0H to 48H
ps_genus_rel <- transform_sample_counts(ps_genus, function(x) x / sum(x))

# Extract data
otu_mat <- as.matrix(otu_table(ps_genus_rel))
if (!taxa_are_rows(ps_genus_rel)) {
  otu_mat <- t(otu_mat)
}

tax_df <- as.data.frame(tax_table(ps_genus_rel))
meta_df <- data.frame(sample_data(ps_genus_rel)) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("SampleID")

# Create long format data
alluvial_data_raw <- otu_mat %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("ASV") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-ASV, names_to = "SampleID", values_to = "Abundance") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    tax_df %>% tibble::rownames_to_column("ASV") %>% dplyr::select(ASV, Genus),
    by = "ASV"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    meta_df %>% dplyr::select(SampleID, timepoint, carbohydrate),
    by = "SampleID"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(timepoint %in% c("0H", "48H"))

# Remove NA values and filter to only valid combinations
alluvial_data_raw_clean <- alluvial_data_raw %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(Abundance),
    !is.na(Genus),
    !is.na(timepoint),
    !is.na(carbohydrate)
  )

# Group by Genus, timepoint, carbohydrate to get mean abundance
# Use na.rm = TRUE to handle any remaining edge cases
alluvial_data_grouped <- alluvial_data_raw_clean %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Genus, timepoint, carbohydrate) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(mean_abundance = mean(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Get top 12 genera for visualization (use max abundance across all timepoints/carbs)
# But don't filter the data yet - we'll use all data and then aggregate
top_genera_by_abundance <- alluvial_data_grouped %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Genus) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(max_abund = max(mean_abundance), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(max_abund)) %>%
  head(12) %>%
  dplyr::pull(Genus)

# Define genera that are important from DA analysis and should be included
# Check with single underscore "g_", double underscore "g__", and without prefix
# since taxonomy formats may vary (tax_table uses "g__" format)
da_important_genera <- c(
  "g_Fusicatenibacter",
  "g__Fusicatenibacter",
  "Fusicatenibacter",
  "g_Fusicatenibacters",
  "g__Fusicatenibacters",
  "Fusicatenibacters",
  "g_Hungatella",
  "g__Hungatella",
  "Hungatella",
  "g_Eggerthella",
  "g__Eggerthella",
  "Eggerthella",
  "g_Peptoniphilus",
  "g__Peptoniphilus",
  "Peptoniphilus"
)

# Check which of these genera exist in the data
# IMPORTANT: Get available_genera from the original tax_table, not from grouped data
# This ensures we find all genera in the taxonomy, even if they have zero/low abundance
available_genera_from_tax <- unique(tax_df$Genus)
available_genera_grouped <- unique(alluvial_data_grouped$Genus)

# Check exact matches first
da_genera_in_data <- da_important_genera[da_important_genera %in% available_genera_from_tax]

# Also check for variations in the full taxonomy (e.g., "g__Fusicatenibacter sp." might be stored differently)
# This will catch any genus containing these names, regardless of prefix or suffix
da_genera_variations <- available_genera_from_tax[
  stringr::str_detect(available_genera_from_tax, regex("Fusicatenibacter|Hungatella|Eggerthella|Peptoniphilus", ignore_case = TRUE))
]

# Combine exact matches and variations
da_genera_found <- unique(c(da_genera_in_data, da_genera_variations))

# Combine top 12 by abundance with DA-important genera
# Remove duplicates and keep up to 16 genera total
top_genera_alluvial <- unique(c(top_genera_by_abundance, da_genera_found))
if (length(top_genera_alluvial) > 16) {
  # If we have more than 16, prioritize top 12 by abundance, then add DA genera
  top_genera_alluvial <- c(
    top_genera_by_abundance,
    setdiff(da_genera_found, top_genera_by_abundance)
  )[1:min(16, length(top_genera_alluvial))]
}

# Filter to top genera and add "Other" category
# Use the grouped data (which has mean abundance per Genus × timepoint × carbohydrate)
# IMPORTANT: Use ALL data from alluvial_data_grouped (not filtered), so we preserve
# low-abundance combinations like RDC 0H
# Replace NaN with 0 before aggregating
alluvial_plot_data_pre_complete <- alluvial_data_grouped %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    mean_abundance = ifelse(is.nan(mean_abundance) | is.na(mean_abundance), 0, mean_abundance),
    Genus_grouped = ifelse(Genus %in% top_genera_alluvial, as.character(Genus), "Other")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Genus_grouped, timepoint, carbohydrate) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(Abundance = sum(mean_abundance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Abundance = ifelse(is.nan(Abundance) | is.na(Abundance), 0, Abundance)
  )

# Ensure we have data for both timepoints for each carbohydrate AND all Genus_grouped values
alluvial_plot_data <- alluvial_plot_data_pre_complete %>%
  tidyr::complete(
    Genus_grouped = c(top_genera_alluvial, "Other"),
    timepoint = c("0H", "48H"),
    carbohydrate = c("No Added Carb", "RDC", "SDC"),
    fill = list(Abundance = 0)
  )

# Create color palette
genus_colors <- c(
  scico::scico(length(top_genera_alluvial), palette = "batlow"),
  "Other" = "grey80"
)
names(genus_colors)[1:length(top_genera_alluvial)] <- top_genera_alluvial

# Create alluvial plots for each carbohydrate
plot_list_alluvial <- list()

for (carb in c("No Added Carb", "RDC", "SDC")) {
  plot_data <- alluvial_plot_data %>%
    dplyr::filter(carbohydrate == carb)
  
  # Ensure both timepoints exist, even if one has zero abundance (fix for RDC panel)
  # Get all unique Genus_grouped values first
  all_genera <- unique(plot_data$Genus_grouped)
  plot_data <- plot_data %>%
    tidyr::complete(
      Genus_grouped = all_genera,
      timepoint = c("0H", "48H"),
      fill = list(Abundance = 0, carbohydrate = carb)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Genus_grouped = factor(
        Genus_grouped,
        levels = c(top_genera_alluvial[top_genera_alluvial %in% unique(Genus_grouped)], "Other")
      ),
      timepoint = factor(timepoint, levels = c("0H", "48H")),
      carbohydrate = carb
    )
  
  p <- ggplot(
    plot_data,
    aes(
      x = timepoint,
      y = Abundance,
      alluvium = Genus_grouped,
      stratum = Genus_grouped,
      fill = Genus_grouped
    )
  ) +
    geom_alluvium(alpha = 0.7, width = 0.3) +
    geom_stratum(width = 0.3, alpha = 0.9) +
    stat_stratum(
      geom = "text",
      aes(label = Genus_grouped),
      size = 2.3,
      fontface = "bold"
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = genus_colors) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.3, 0.3))) +
    labs(
      title = carb,
      x = "Timepoint",
      y = "Relative Abundance",
      fill = "Genus"
    ) +
    theme_scfa() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
    )
  
  plot_list_alluvial[[carb]] <- p
}

# Combine plots using patchwork
combined_alluvial <- wrap_plots(plot_list_alluvial, ncol = 3) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Genus Composition Changes from 0H to 48H by Carbohydrate Type",
    subtitle = paste0("Flow diagram showing relative abundance changes (top ", length(top_genera_alluvial), " genera including DA-important taxa)"),
    theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"))
  )

print(combined_alluvial)
```

```{r genus-validation, echo=FALSE, fig.width=14, fig.height=10}
)

available_genera_grouped <- unique(genus_summary_all$Genus)

# This will catch any genus containing these names, regardless of prefix or suffix

]
```

## 6.5 Differential Abundance and Predictive Modeling

Differential abundance analysis identifies microbial taxa that differ significantly between experimental conditions. We applied multiple complementary methods to ensure robust identification of differentially abundant taxa: ANCOM-BC2 (Analysis of Compositions of Microbiomes with Bias Correction), which accounts for compositional bias and uses mixed-effects models; MaAsLin2 (Microbiome Multivariable Associations with Linear Models), which handles multivariate associations with normalization and transformations; and LEfSe (Linear Discriminant Analysis Effect Size), which identifies biomarker taxa between groups.

### 6.5.1 ANCOM-BC2 Analysis

ANCOM-BC2 models microbial abundance using a generalized linear mixed-effects model with bias correction for compositional data. We tested the main effects of group (Healthy vs Obese), carbohydrate type (RDC vs No Added Carb, SDC vs No Added Carb), timepoint (48H vs 0H), and their interactions.

```{r ancombc2-analysis, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, cache.path="cache/integrated-"}
# Prepare phyloseq object for ANCOM-BC2 (needs count data, not relative)
# Use ps (counts) and ensure we have genus-level data
ps_ancombc2 <- ps_genus

# Remove samples with too many zeros that cause estimation issues
zero_prop <- apply(otu_table(ps_ancombc2), 2, function(x) sum(x == 0) / length(x))
problematic_samples <- names(zero_prop[zero_prop > 0.95])

if (length(problematic_samples) > 0) {
  ps_ancombc2_clean <- subset_samples(ps_ancombc2, !sample_names(ps_ancombc2) %in% problematic_samples)
} else {
  ps_ancombc2_clean <- ps_ancombc2
}

# Check if we have enough samples
if (nsamples(ps_ancombc2_clean) < 10) {
  cat("WARNING: Insufficient samples for ANCOM-BC2 analysis\n")
  ancombc2_res <- NULL
} else {
  # Run ANCOM-BC2 with mixed-effects model
  ancombc2_res <- tryCatch({
    ANCOMBC::ancombc2(
      data = ps_ancombc2_clean,
      tax_level = "Genus",
      fix_formula = "group + carbohydrate * timepoint",
      rand_formula = "(1|subject_id)",
      p_adj_method = "BH",
      prv_cut = 0.10,
      lib_cut = 0,
      s0_perc = 0.05,
      group = "carbohydrate",
      struc_zero = TRUE,
      neg_lb = TRUE,
      alpha = 0.05,
      global = TRUE
    )
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("ANCOM-BC2 failed:", e$message, "\n")
    NULL
  })
}

# Extract results if available
if (!is.null(ancombc2_res) && !is.null(ancombc2_res$res)) {
  res_data <- ancombc2_res$res
  
  # Get the effect names
  effect_names <- c("groupObese", "carbohydrateRDC", "carbohydrateSDC", "timepoint48H", 
                    "carbohydrateRDC:timepoint48H", "carbohydrateSDC:timepoint48H")
  
  # Create a data frame from the results for each effect
  ancombc2_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(effect_names, function(effect) {
    lfc_col <- paste0("lfc_", effect)
    se_col <- paste0("se_", effect)
    W_col <- paste0("W_", effect)
    p_col <- paste0("p_", effect)
    q_col <- paste0("q_", effect)
    diff_col <- paste0("diff_", effect)
    
    if (all(c(lfc_col, se_col, W_col, p_col, q_col, diff_col) %in% colnames(res_data))) {
      tibble(
        taxon = res_data$taxon,
        effect = effect,
        beta = res_data[[lfc_col]],
        se = res_data[[se_col]],
        W = res_data[[W_col]],
        p_value = res_data[[p_col]],
        q_value = res_data[[q_col]],
        diff_abn = res_data[[diff_col]]
      )
    } else {
      tibble()
    }
  }) %>% dplyr::arrange(q_value)
} else {
  ancombc2_tbl <- tibble(
    taxon = character(0),
    effect = character(0),
    beta = numeric(0),
    se = numeric(0),
    W = numeric(0),
    p_value = numeric(0),
    q_value = numeric(0),
    diff_abn = logical(0)
  )
  cat("No ANCOM-BC2 results available - analysis may have failed\n")
}

# Show summary of significant results
if (nrow(ancombc2_tbl) > 0 && "q_value" %in% names(ancombc2_tbl)) {
  ancombc2_sig <- ancombc2_tbl %>% dplyr::filter(q_value < 0.1)
  cat("ANCOM-BC2 significant results (q < 0.1):", nrow(ancombc2_sig), "taxon-effect combinations\n")
}
```

### 6.5.2 ANCOM-BC2 Forest Plots

```{r ancombc2-forest-plot, echo=FALSE, fig.width=16, fig.height=12}
# Prepare data for forest plot
if (nrow(ancombc2_tbl) > 0 && "q_value" %in% names(ancombc2_tbl)) {
  forest_data <- ancombc2_tbl %>%
    dplyr::filter(q_value < 0.1) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      # Calculate confidence intervals
      ci_lower = beta - 1.96 * se,
      ci_upper = beta + 1.96 * se,
      # Create effect labels
      effect_label = dplyr::case_when(
        effect == "groupObese" ~ "Group: Obese vs Healthy",
        effect == "carbohydrateRDC" ~ "Carbohydrate: RDC vs No Added Carb",
        effect == "carbohydrateSDC" ~ "Carbohydrate: SDC vs No Added Carb", 
        effect == "timepoint48H" ~ "Timepoint: 48H vs 0H",
        effect == "carbohydrateRDC:timepoint48H" ~ "RDC × 48H Interaction",
        effect == "carbohydrateSDC:timepoint48H" ~ "SDC × 48H Interaction",
        TRUE ~ effect
      ),
      # Create taxon labels (remove g__ prefix for cleaner display)
      taxon_label = stringr::str_replace(taxon, "^g__", ""),
      # Color by significance level
      significance = dplyr::case_when(
        q_value < 0.001 ~ "q < 0.001",
        q_value < 0.01 ~ "q < 0.01", 
        q_value < 0.05 ~ "q < 0.05",
        q_value < 0.1 ~ "q < 0.1",
        TRUE ~ "q ≥ 0.1"
      )
    ) %>%
    # Order by effect size (absolute value)
    dplyr::arrange(desc(abs(beta)))
  
  if (nrow(forest_data) > 0) {
    # Create forest plot
    ancombc2_forest_plot <- ggplot(forest_data, aes(x = beta, y = reorder(taxon_label, beta))) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
      geom_point(aes(color = significance), size = 2) +
      geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = ci_lower, xmax = ci_upper, color = significance), 
                     height = 0.2, alpha = 0.8) +
      facet_wrap(~ effect_label, scales = "free_x", ncol = 2) +
      scale_color_manual(
        values = c("q < 0.001" = "#d73027", 
                   "q < 0.01" = "#f46d43",
                   "q < 0.05" = "#fdae61", 
                   "q < 0.1" = "#fee08b"),
        name = "FDR-adjusted\np-value"
      ) +
      labs(
        title = "ANCOM-BC2 Results: Forest Plot of Significant Taxa",
        subtitle = "Effect sizes (log-fold changes) with 95% confidence intervals",
        x = "Log-fold change (β)",
        y = "Genus"
      ) +
      theme_scfa() +
      theme(
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
      )
    
    print(ancombc2_forest_plot)
  } else {
    cat("No significant ANCOM-BC2 results found (q < 0.1) for forest plot\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("No ANCOM-BC2 results available for forest plot - analysis may have failed\n")
}
```

### 6.5.3 ANCOM-BC2 Side-by-Side Comparison: Carbohydrate Effects

```{r ancombc2-carb-comparison, echo=FALSE, fig.width=14, fig.height=10}
# Compare RDC vs No Carb and SDC vs No Carb effects side by side
if (nrow(ancombc2_tbl) > 0 && "effect" %in% names(ancombc2_tbl)) {
  comparison_data <- ancombc2_tbl %>%
    dplyr::filter(effect %in% c("carbohydrateRDC", "carbohydrateSDC")) %>%
    dplyr::select(taxon, effect, beta, se, p_value, q_value, diff_abn) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(
      names_from = effect,
      values_from = c(beta, se, p_value, q_value, diff_abn),
      names_sep = "_"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      # Calculate difference between RDC and SDC effects
      effect_difference = beta_carbohydrateRDC - beta_carbohydrateSDC,
      # Determine which treatment has stronger effect
      stronger_effect = dplyr::case_when(
        abs(beta_carbohydrateRDC) > abs(beta_carbohydrateSDC) ~ "RDC",
        abs(beta_carbohydrateSDC) > abs(beta_carbohydrateRDC) ~ "SDC",
        TRUE ~ "Equal"
      ),
      # Check if effects are opposite (different signs)
      opposite_effects = sign(beta_carbohydrateRDC) != sign(beta_carbohydrateSDC),
      # Check if either effect is significant
      either_significant = (q_value_carbohydrateRDC < 0.1) | (q_value_carbohydrateSDC < 0.1),
      # Clean taxon names
      taxon_clean = stringr::str_replace(taxon, "^g__", "")
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(either_significant | opposite_effects) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(desc(abs(effect_difference)))
  
  if (nrow(comparison_data) > 0) {
    # Prepare long format for plotting
    comparison_plot_data <- comparison_data %>%
      dplyr::select(taxon_clean, beta_carbohydrateRDC, beta_carbohydrateSDC, 
                    se_carbohydrateRDC, se_carbohydrateSDC,
                    q_value_carbohydrateRDC, q_value_carbohydrateSDC) %>%
      tidyr::pivot_longer(
        cols = c(beta_carbohydrateRDC, beta_carbohydrateSDC),
        names_to = "treatment",
        values_to = "beta",
        names_prefix = "beta_"
      ) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        se = dplyr::case_when(
          treatment == "carbohydrateRDC" ~ se_carbohydrateRDC,
          treatment == "carbohydrateSDC" ~ se_carbohydrateSDC,
          TRUE ~ NA_real_
        ),
        q_value = dplyr::case_when(
          treatment == "carbohydrateRDC" ~ q_value_carbohydrateRDC,
          treatment == "carbohydrateSDC" ~ q_value_carbohydrateSDC,
          TRUE ~ NA_real_
        ),
        ci_lower = beta - 1.96 * se,
        ci_upper = beta + 1.96 * se,
        treatment_label = dplyr::case_when(
          treatment == "carbohydrateRDC" ~ "RDC vs No Added Carb",
          treatment == "carbohydrateSDC" ~ "SDC vs No Added Carb",
          TRUE ~ treatment
        ),
        significance = dplyr::case_when(
          q_value < 0.001 ~ "q < 0.001",
          q_value < 0.01 ~ "q < 0.01",
          q_value < 0.05 ~ "q < 0.05",
          q_value < 0.1 ~ "q < 0.1",
          TRUE ~ "q ≥ 0.1"
        )
      )
    
    ancombc2_comparison_plot <- ggplot(
      comparison_plot_data,
      aes(x = beta, y = reorder(taxon_clean, beta))
    ) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
      geom_point(aes(color = significance), size = 2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
      geom_errorbarh(
        aes(xmin = ci_lower, xmax = ci_upper, color = significance),
        height = 0.2,
        alpha = 0.8,
        position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)
      ) +
      facet_wrap(~ treatment_label, ncol = 2) +
      scale_color_manual(
        values = c("q < 0.001" = "#d73027", 
                   "q < 0.01" = "#f46d43",
                   "q < 0.05" = "#fdae61", 
                   "q < 0.1" = "#fee08b",
                   "q ≥ 0.1" = "gray70"),
        name = "FDR-adjusted\np-value"
      ) +
      labs(
        title = "ANCOM-BC2: Side-by-Side Comparison of Carbohydrate Effects",
        subtitle = "RDC vs No Added Carb and SDC vs No Added Carb",
        x = "Log-fold change (β)",
        y = "Genus"
      ) +
      theme_scfa() +
      theme(
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "bottom"
      )
    
    print(ancombc2_comparison_plot)
  } else {
    cat("No significant comparisons found for side-by-side plot\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("No ANCOM-BC2 results available for comparison\n")
}
```
