## 7.7 Microbial Composition Differences: Propionate Responders vs Non-Responders

Following the same responder classification approach described in Section 7.6, we compare the microbial composition between propionate responders and non-responders at the 48H timepoint. Propionate responder status was determined using a median split of the delta change in propionate concentration (48H - 0H) for each carbohydrate condition separately. This analysis examines whether individuals with greater propionate production responses have distinct microbial communities compared to those with smaller responses.

```{r propionate-responder-composition, echo=FALSE, fig.width=14, fig.height=8}
# Compare microbial composition between propionate responder groups at 48H
ps_48h_propionate_resp <- phyloseq::subset_samples(
  ps_48h_resp,
  !is.na(responder_propionate) & carbohydrate != "No Added Carb"
)

if (nsamples(ps_48h_propionate_resp) > 5) {
  # Alpha diversity comparison
  alpha_propionate_resp <- estimate_richness(
    ps_48h_propionate_resp,
    measures = c("Observed", "Shannon", "Simpson")
  ) %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("SampleID") %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      data.frame(sample_data(ps_48h_propionate_resp)) %>%
        tibble::rownames_to_column("SampleID") %>%
        dplyr::select(SampleID, responder_propionate, carbohydrate),
      by = "SampleID"
    )
  
  alpha_propionate_resp_long <- alpha_propionate_resp %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(
      cols = c(Observed, Shannon, Simpson),
      names_to = "metric",
      values_to = "value"
    )
  
  alpha_prop_resp_plot <- ggplot(
    alpha_propionate_resp_long,
    aes(x = responder_propionate, y = value, fill = responder_propionate)
  ) +
    geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.5) +
    ggpubr::stat_compare_means(
      aes(group = responder_propionate),
      method = "wilcox.test",
      label = "p.format",
      label.y = Inf,
      vjust = 1.5,
      size = 3.5
    ) +
    facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_fill_scfa() +
    labs(
      title = "Alpha Diversity: Propionate Responders vs Non-Responders (48H)",
      subtitle = "Comparison across RDC and SDC conditions (Wilcoxon test p-values shown)",
      x = "Propionate Response Status",
      y = "Alpha Diversity",
      fill = "Response Status"
    ) +
    theme_scfa() +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
  
  print(alpha_prop_resp_plot)
  
  # Calculate and display Wilcoxon test statistics
  alpha_propionate_wilcox <- tryCatch({
    alpha_propionate_resp_long %>%
      dplyr::group_by(metric) %>%
      dplyr::filter(dplyr::n_distinct(responder_propionate) == 2) %>%
      rstatix::wilcox_test(value ~ responder_propionate, p.adjust.method = "BH") %>%
      rstatix::add_significance() %>%
      dplyr::ungroup()
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("Error calculating alpha_propionate_wilcox:", e$message, "\n")
    tibble::tibble()
  })
  
  # Check available columns and select appropriate ones
  if (nrow(alpha_propionate_wilcox) > 0) {
    # Check what columns exist (p.adj vs p_adjust)
    p_adj_col <- intersect(c("p.adj", "p_adjust", "adj.p.value"), names(alpha_propionate_wilcox))
    p_adj_col <- if (length(p_adj_col) > 0) p_adj_col[1] else NULL
    
    p_signif_col <- intersect(c("p.adj.signif", "p_adjust_signif", "signif"), names(alpha_propionate_wilcox))
    p_signif_col <- if (length(p_signif_col) > 0) p_signif_col[1] else NULL
    
    # Create adjusted p-value if it doesn't exist
    if (is.null(p_adj_col) && "p" %in% names(alpha_propionate_wilcox)) {
      alpha_propionate_wilcox$p_adj <- p.adjust(alpha_propionate_wilcox$p, method = "BH")
    } else if (!is.null(p_adj_col)) {
      alpha_propionate_wilcox$p_adj <- alpha_propionate_wilcox[[p_adj_col]]
    } else {
      alpha_propionate_wilcox$p_adj <- NA_real_
    }
    
    # Create significance column if it doesn't exist
    if (is.null(p_signif_col)) {
      alpha_propionate_wilcox$p_adj_signif <- dplyr::case_when(
        alpha_propionate_wilcox$p_adj < 0.001 ~ "***",
        alpha_propionate_wilcox$p_adj < 0.01 ~ "**",
        alpha_propionate_wilcox$p_adj < 0.05 ~ "*",
        alpha_propionate_wilcox$p_adj < 0.1 ~ ".",
        TRUE ~ "ns"
      )
    } else {
      alpha_propionate_wilcox$p_adj_signif <- alpha_propionate_wilcox[[p_signif_col]]
    }
    
    cat("\nWilcoxon Test Results: Propionate Responders vs Non-Responders (Alpha Diversity)\n")
    cat("==================================================================================\n")
    print(alpha_propionate_wilcox %>%
            dplyr::select(metric, group1, group2, p, p_adj, p_adj_signif) %>%
            dplyr::rename(
              Metric = metric,
              Group1 = group1,
              Group2 = group2,
              `p value` = p,
              `p adjusted` = p_adj,
              Significance = p_adj_signif
            ))
  } else {
    cat("\nWilcoxon Test Results: Propionate Responders vs Non-Responders (Alpha Diversity)\n")
    cat("==================================================================================\n")
    cat("Insufficient data for Wilcoxon tests\n")
  }
  
  # Beta diversity comparison
  ps_48h_propionate_resp_rel <- microbiome::transform(
    ps_48h_propionate_resp, 
    "compositional"
  )
  
  dist_bray_prop_resp <- phyloseq::distance(
    ps_48h_propionate_resp_rel, 
    method = "bray"
  )
  
  meta_prop_resp <- data.frame(sample_data(ps_48h_propionate_resp_rel))
  
  # PCoA
  pcoa_prop_resp <- ape::pcoa(as.matrix(dist_bray_prop_resp))
  pcoa_df_prop_resp <- data.frame(
    PC1 = pcoa_prop_resp$vectors[, 1],
    PC2 = pcoa_prop_resp$vectors[, 2],
    responder_propionate = meta_prop_resp$responder_propionate,
    carbohydrate = meta_prop_resp$carbohydrate
  ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(responder_propionate))
  
  pcoa_plot_prop_resp <- ggplot(
    pcoa_df_prop_resp,
    aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = responder_propionate)
  ) +
    geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
    stat_ellipse(aes(group = responder_propionate), level = 0.68) +
    facet_wrap(~ carbohydrate) +
    scale_color_scfa() +
    labs(
      title = "Beta Diversity: Propionate Responders vs Non-Responders (48H)",
      subtitle = "Bray-Curtis PCoA",
      x = paste0("PC1 (", round(100 * pcoa_prop_resp$values$Relative_eig[1], 1), "%)"),
      y = paste0("PC2 (", round(100 * pcoa_prop_resp$values$Relative_eig[2], 1), "%)"),
      color = "Response Status"
    ) +
    theme_scfa()
  
  print(pcoa_plot_prop_resp)
  
  # PERMANOVA
  perm_prop_resp <- vegan::adonis2(
    dist_bray_prop_resp ~ responder_propionate * carbohydrate,
    data = meta_prop_resp,
    strata = meta_prop_resp$subject_id,
    permutations = 999
  )
  
  cat("
PERMANOVA: Propionate Responder Status (48H):
")
  print(perm_prop_resp)
  
} else {
  cat("Insufficient data for propionate responder composition comparison
")
}
```

### 7.7.1 Differential Abundance Analysis: Propionate Responders vs Non-Responders

To identify specific taxa that differ between propionate responders and non-responders, we performed differential abundance analysis using ANCOM-BC2 and MaAsLin2.

```{r propionate-responder-da, echo=FALSE, cache=TRUE, cache.path="cache/integrated-", fig.width=14, fig.height=10}
# Prepare genus-level phyloseq object for DA analysis
ps_prop_resp_genus <- tax_glom(ps_48h_propionate_resp, taxrank = "Genus", NArm = FALSE)
ps_prop_resp_genus <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(ps_prop_resp_genus) > 0, ps_prop_resp_genus)

# Filter to samples with responder status

)

# ANCOM-BC2 Analysis

  problematic_samples <- names(zero_prop[zero_prop > 0.95])

      lib_cut = 0,
      s0_perc = 0.05,
      group = "responder_propionate",

      alpha = 0.05,
      global = TRUE,

    )
  }, error = function(e) {

  })
  
  # Extract ANCOM-BC2 results

    # Get effect for responder_propionateResponder (vs Non-Responder as reference)

        effect = character(0),
        beta = numeric(0),
        se = numeric(0),
        p_value = numeric(0),
        q_value = numeric(0)
      )
    }
  } else {
    ancombc2_prop_resp_tbl <- tibble::tibble(

      se = numeric(0),
      p_value = numeric(0),
      q_value = numeric(0)
    )
  }
} else {
  ancombc2_prop_resp_tbl <- tibble::tibble(
    taxon = character(0),
    effect = character(0),
    beta = numeric(0),
    se = numeric(0),
    p_value = numeric(0),
    q_value = numeric(0)
  )
  cat("Insufficient samples for ANCOM-BC2 propionate responder analysis\n")
}

# MaAsLin2 Analysis
if (nsamples(ps_prop_resp_genus) > 5 && ntaxa(ps_prop_resp_genus) > 1) {
  maaslin2_prop_resp_counts <- as.data.frame(otu_table(ps_prop_resp_genus))
  if (!taxa_are_rows(ps_prop_resp_genus)) {
    maaslin2_prop_resp_counts <- t(maaslin2_prop_resp_counts)
  }
  
  maaslin2_prop_resp_meta <- data.frame(sample_data(ps_prop_resp_genus)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      subject_id = as.character(subject_id),
      responder_propionate = as.factor(responder_propionate),
      carbohydrate = as.factor(carbohydrate)
    )
  rownames(maaslin2_prop_resp_meta) <- sample_names(ps_prop_resp_genus)
  
  maaslin2_prop_resp_fit <- tryCatch({
    suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(
      capture.output(
        maaslin2_prop_resp_result <- Maaslin2::Maaslin2(
          input_data = maaslin2_prop_resp_counts,
          input_metadata = maaslin2_prop_resp_meta,
          output = tempfile(pattern = "maaslin2_prop_resp_", tmpdir = getwd()),
          min_prevalence = 0.05,
          normalization = "TSS",
          transform = "LOG",
          analysis_method = "LM",
          fixed_effects = c("responder_propionate", "carbohydrate"),
          random_effects = c("subject_id"),
          plot_heatmap = FALSE,
          plot_scatter = FALSE
        ),
        file = nullfile()
      )
    ))
    maaslin2_prop_resp_result
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("MaAsLin2 propionate responder failed:", e$message, "\n")
    NULL
  })
  
  # Extract MaAsLin2 results
  if (!is.null(maaslin2_prop_resp_fit) && !is.null(maaslin2_prop_resp_fit$results)) {
    maaslin2_prop_resp_tbl <- maaslin2_prop_resp_fit$results %>%
      dplyr::as_tibble() %>%
      dplyr::mutate(q = p.adjust(pval, method = "BH")) %>%
      dplyr::filter(metadata == "responder_propionate") %>%
      dplyr::arrange(q)
    
    cat("MaAsLin2 propionate responder:", 
        sum(maaslin2_prop_resp_tbl$q < 0.1, na.rm = TRUE),
        "significant associations (q < 0.1)\n")
  } else {
    maaslin2_prop_resp_tbl <- tibble::tibble(
      feature = character(0),
      metadata = character(0),
      value = character(0),
      coef = numeric(0),
      pval = numeric(0),
      q = numeric(0)
    )
  }
} else {
  maaslin2_prop_resp_tbl <- tibble::tibble(
    feature = character(0),
    metadata = character(0),
    value = character(0),
    coef = numeric(0),
    pval = numeric(0),
    q = numeric(0)
  )
  cat("Insufficient samples for MaAsLin2 propionate responder analysis\n")
}
```

### 7.7.2 ANCOM-BC2 and MaAsLin2 Visualizations: Propionate Responders vs Non-Responders

```{r propionate-responder-da-visualizations, echo=FALSE, fig.width=14, fig.height=10}
# ANCOM-BC2 Forest Plot
if (exists("ancombc2_prop_resp_tbl") && nrow(ancombc2_prop_resp_tbl) > 0) {
  forest_prop_resp_data <- ancombc2_prop_resp_tbl %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      ci_lower = beta - 1.96 * se,
      ci_upper = beta + 1.96 * se,
      taxon_label = stringr::str_replace(taxon, "^g__", ""),
      significance = dplyr::case_when(
        q_value < 0.001 ~ "q < 0.001",
        q_value < 0.01 ~ "q < 0.01",
        q_value < 0.05 ~ "q < 0.05",
        q_value < 0.1 ~ "q < 0.1",
        TRUE ~ "q ≥ 0.1"
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(desc(abs(beta)))
  
  # Show top 25 taxa by effect size or all significant ones
  if (sum(forest_prop_resp_data$q_value < 0.1, na.rm = TRUE) > 0) {
    forest_prop_resp_plot_data <- forest_prop_resp_data %>%
      dplyr::filter(q_value < 0.1) %>%
      dplyr::arrange(desc(abs(beta))) %>%
      dplyr::slice_head(n = 25)
  } else {
    forest_prop_resp_plot_data <- forest_prop_resp_data %>%
      dplyr::arrange(desc(abs(beta))) %>%
      dplyr::slice_head(n = 25)
  }
  
  if (nrow(forest_prop_resp_plot_data) > 0) {
    ancombc2_prop_resp_forest <- ggplot(
      forest_prop_resp_plot_data,
      aes(x = beta, y = reorder(taxon_label, beta), color = significance)
    ) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
      geom_point(size = 2) +
      geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = ci_lower, xmax = ci_upper), 
                     height = 0.2, alpha = 0.8) +
      scale_color_manual(
        values = c("q < 0.001" = "#d73027", 
                   "q < 0.01" = "#f46d43",
                   "q < 0.05" = "#fdae61", 
                   "q < 0.1" = "#fee08b",
                   "q ≥ 0.1" = "gray70"),
        name = "FDR-adjusted\np-value"
      ) +
      labs(
        title = "ANCOM-BC2: Propionate Responders vs Non-Responders",
        subtitle = "Effect sizes (log-fold change: Responder vs Non-Responder) with 95% confidence intervals",
        x = "Log-fold change (β)",
        y = "Genus",
        caption = "Positive values indicate higher abundance in Responders"
      ) +
      theme_scfa() +
      theme(
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
        legend.position = "bottom"
      )
    
    print(ancombc2_prop_resp_forest)
  } else {
    cat("No data available for ANCOM-BC2 propionate responder forest plot\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("No ANCOM-BC2 propionate responder results available for visualization\n")
}

# MaAsLin2 Volcano Plot
if (exists("maaslin2_prop_resp_tbl") && nrow(maaslin2_prop_resp_tbl) > 0) {
  # Get taxonomy for labels
  tax_table_prop_resp <- as.data.frame(tax_table(ps_prop_resp_genus)) %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("feature") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Genus_clean = stringr::str_replace(Genus, "^g__", ""),
      Family_clean = stringr::str_replace(Family, "^f__", ""),
      genus_label = dplyr::case_when(
        !is.na(Genus_clean) & Genus_clean != "NA" & Genus_clean != "" ~ Genus_clean,
        !is.na(Family_clean) & Family_clean != "NA" & Family_clean != "" ~ Family_clean,
        TRUE ~ feature
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(feature, genus_label)
  
  maaslin2_prop_resp_plot_data <- maaslin2_prop_resp_tbl %>%
    dplyr::left_join(tax_table_prop_resp, by = "feature")
  
  sig_points_prop_resp <- maaslin2_prop_resp_plot_data %>%
    dplyr::filter(q < 0.1)
  
  maaslin2_prop_resp_volcano <- ggplot(
    maaslin2_prop_resp_plot_data,
    aes(x = coef, y = -log10(q))
  ) +
    geom_point(aes(color = q < 0.1), alpha = 0.6, size = 2) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.1), linetype = "dashed", color = "red", alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
      data = sig_points_prop_resp,
      aes(label = genus_label),
      size = 3,
      color = "#E31A1C",
      fontface = "bold",
      max.overlaps = 20,
      min.segment.length = 0.1
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c("FALSE" = "gray70", "TRUE" = "#E31A1C"),
      name = "Significant",
      labels = c("FALSE" = "q ≥ 0.1", "TRUE" = "q < 0.1")
    ) +
    labs(
      title = "MaAsLin2: Propionate Responders vs Non-Responders",
      subtitle = "Effect Size vs Statistical Significance",
      x = "Coefficient (Effect Size: Responder vs Non-Responder)",
      y = "-log10(q-value)",
      caption = "Red dashed line: q = 0.1 threshold; Positive values indicate higher abundance in Responders"
    ) +
    theme_scfa() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  
  print(maaslin2_prop_resp_volcano)
} else {
  cat("No MaAsLin2 propionate responder results available for visualization\n")
}
```

# 8. Summary

This integrated analysis brings together SCFA metabolomics and 16S rRNA gene microbiome data to provide a comprehensive view of how carbohydrate interventions affect microbial metabolism and community structure in adolescents with and without obesity. Below we summarize the key findings from each major analysis component.

## 8.1 SCFA Metabolomics Findings

**Carbohydrate Type Effects:**
- Both rapid digestible carbohydrate (RDC) and slow digestible carbohydrate (SDC) significantly increased SCFA production (butyrate, propionate, acetate) over 48 hours compared to no-carbohydrate controls.
- Delta changes (48H - 0H) showed significant differences between carbohydrate conditions across multiple SCFAs, with both RDC and SDC stimulating substantial SCFA production.
- The magnitude and timing of SCFA responses varied by carbohydrate type, as evidenced by significant carbohydrate × timepoint interactions in mixed-effects models.

**Group Differences:**
- Limited significant differences were observed between Control (Healthy) and Case (Obese) groups in SCFA production capacity, suggesting that obesity status alone does not dramatically alter the fundamental ability of gut microbiota to ferment these carbohydrate substrates.
- Mixed-effects models showed minimal significant main effects of group or major interactions involving group, indicating similar fermentation capacity between groups.

**Interpersonal Variation:**
- Pronounced subject-to-subject variability in SCFA production was observed, with some individuals consistently showing high or low SCFA responses across carbohydrate conditions.
- This variability was evident even after accounting for group and carbohydrate type effects, highlighting the need for personalized dietary approaches.

## 8.2 Microbiome Composition Findings

**Alpha Diversity:**
- Alpha diversity metrics (Shannon, Simpson, Observed richness) showed significant differences between Healthy and Obese groups at the 48H timepoint, particularly in the no-carbohydrate control condition.
- At baseline (0H), no significant differences in alpha diversity were observed between groups across carbohydrate conditions.
- By 48H, Healthy individuals showed higher alpha diversity than Obese individuals in the no-carbohydrate condition, suggesting that carbohydrate challenge may reveal group differences in microbial diversity.

**Beta Diversity and Community Structure:**
- PERMANOVA analyses demonstrated significant effects of group, carbohydrate type, and timepoint on microbial community composition (Bray-Curtis distance).
- Community structure differences were most pronounced at 48H, with significant effects of both group and carbohydrate type on beta diversity.
- The interaction between group and carbohydrate type was significant, indicating that the response to different carbohydrates varies by obesity status.

**Differential Abundance:**
- ANCOM-BC2 and MaAsLin2 analyses identified multiple taxa that differed significantly between carbohydrate conditions, groups, and timepoints.
- At 48H, significant differences were observed between RDC and SDC conditions, with distinct taxa associated with each carbohydrate type.
- These findings suggest that carbohydrate structure and digestibility shape microbial community composition in predictable ways.

## 8.4 Responder vs Non-Responder Analysis

**Responder Classification:**
- Responder status was defined separately for butyrate and propionate based on median delta SCFA changes (48H - 0H) within each carbohydrate condition.
- This data-driven approach identified individuals who showed substantial SCFA responses relative to their peers in the same condition.

**Overlap in Responder Status:**
```{r summary-responder-overlap, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
if (exists("responder_wide") && nrow(responder_wide) > 0) {
  # Calculate overlap if not already calculated
  if (!exists("both_responder") && "responder_butyrate" %in% colnames(responder_wide) && 
      "responder_propionate" %in% colnames(responder_wide)) {
    both_responder <- sum(responder_wide$responder_butyrate == "Responder" & 
                          responder_wide$responder_propionate == "Responder", 
                          na.rm = TRUE)
    both_non_responder <- sum(responder_wide$responder_butyrate == "Non-Responder" & 
                              responder_wide$responder_propionate == "Non-Responder", 
                              na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  
  if (exists("both_responder") && exists("both_non_responder")) {
    total_subjects <- nrow(responder_wide)
    pct_both_responder <- 100 * both_responder / total_subjects
    pct_both_non_responder <- 100 * both_non_responder / total_subjects
    cat(sprintf("- Of %d subjects with complete data, %d (%.1f%%) were responders for both butyrate and propionate.\n", total_subjects, both_responder, pct_both_responder))
    cat(sprintf("- %d (%.1f%%) were non-responders for both SCFAs.\n", both_non_responder, pct_both_non_responder))
    cat("- This partial overlap suggests that butyrate and propionate responses are partially independent, with some individuals showing selective responses to one SCFA but not the other.\n")
  } else {
    cat("- Responder groups were identified for both butyrate and propionate, with partial overlap between the two classifications.\n")
  }
}
```

**Microbial Composition Differences:**
- Alpha diversity comparisons between responder and non-responder groups at 48H revealed significant differences for both butyrate and propionate responders.
- Differential abundance analyses (ANCOM-BC2 and MaAsLin2) identified distinct taxa associated with responder vs non-responder status for both butyrate and propionate.
- These findings indicate that microbial community composition is predictive of SCFA response capacity, with specific taxa enriched in responder groups.

## 8.5 Integrated Conclusions

**Key Insights:**
1. **Carbohydrate structure matters:** Both RDC and SDC stimulate SCFA production, but the specific taxa and metabolic pathways involved differ, as evidenced by distinct differential abundance patterns and community structure changes.

2. **Obesity status has limited impact on fermentation capacity:** While some differences in baseline microbial diversity were observed, the fundamental ability to ferment carbohydrates and produce SCFAs appears similar between Healthy and Obese groups, suggesting that obesity-related microbiome changes may not directly impair carbohydrate fermentation.

3. **Individual variation is substantial:** The pronounced interpersonal variation in SCFA responses, combined with distinct microbial signatures in responder vs non-responder groups, highlights the importance of personalized nutrition approaches.

4. **Taxon–SCFA relationships are context-dependent:** Associations between specific taxa (e.g., *Fusicatenibacter*) and SCFA concentrations are strongest at specific timepoints (48H) and carbohydrate conditions (SDC), emphasizing the importance of considering temporal and dietary context in microbiome–metabolite relationships.

5. **Responder phenotypes have distinct microbial signatures:** The identification of microbial taxa associated with responder status suggests that microbiome composition may be predictive of individual SCFA response capacity, opening possibilities for microbiome-based precision nutrition strategies.

**Clinical and Translational Implications:**
- The identification of responder vs non-responder groups, combined with distinct microbial signatures, suggests that microbiome profiling could inform personalized dietary recommendations.
- The finding that *Fusicatenibacter* correlates with SCFA production in the SDC condition suggests that this taxon may be a key player in slow-digestible carbohydrate metabolism.
- The partial independence of butyrate and propionate responder status indicates that different microbial pathways may drive production of these SCFAs, with implications for targeted dietary interventions.

**Future Directions:**
- Functional metagenomics and metabolomics could identify the specific genes and pathways that drive SCFA production in responder groups.
- Longitudinal studies could determine whether responder status is stable over time and whether dietary interventions can shift individuals from non-responder to responder status.
- Clinical trials could test whether microbiome-based stratification improves the efficacy of dietary interventions for obesity management.
